root_cause.text: In KVM arm64 nested virtualization, the XN permissions helper misused `FIELD_PREP()` on an already-extracted `xn` bitfield in `kvm_s2_trans_exec_el0()` and `kvm_s2_trans_exec_el1()`, so when `!FEAT_XNX` the code masked the wrong value and effectively failed to clear XN[0], granting execute permission unconditionally.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `xn &= FIELD_PREP(KVM_PTE_LEAF_ATTR_HI_S2_XN, 0b10);` to `xn &= 0b10;` in `arch/arm64/include/asm/kvm_nested.h`, and the commit message states that “XN has already been extracted from its bitfield position so using FIELD_PREP() on the mask that clears XN[0] is completely broken, having the effect of unconditionally granting execute permissions.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the EL0 execute-never masking logic to use the correct raw bit mask when XNX is unavailable.
intent_record.what: In kvm_s2_trans_exec_el0(), the expression used to mask `xn` when `kvm_has_xnx(kvm)` is false was changed from `xn &= FIELD_PREP(KVM_PTE_LEAF_ATTR_HI_S2_XN, 0b10);` to `xn &= 0b10;`.
intent_record.how: This changes the masking operation to use the raw bit pattern directly, ensuring `xn` is reduced to only the relevant bit before the subsequent switch. It preserves the intended execution path selection for EL0 execute permissions without relying on the field-preparation macro.

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify the XNX masking logic in kvm_s2_trans_exec_el1() by using a direct bitmask when XNX is unsupported.
intent_record.what: In kvm_s2_trans_exec_el1(), the assignment inside the `if (!kvm_has_xnx(kvm))` block changed from `xn &= FIELD_PREP(KVM_PTE_LEAF_ATTR_HI_S2_XN, 0b10);` to `xn &= 0b10;`.
intent_record.how: This changes the mask applied to `xn` when XNX is not supported, so only the low-bit pattern `0b10` is retained directly instead of using a field-preparation macro. The runtime effect is to preserve the same intended bit filtering while avoiding an unnecessary macro-based mask construction.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes the EL0 XN masking logic when FEAT_XNX is unavailable, which is exactly where FIELD_PREP() was misused and execute permission was wrongly granted.

The change directly targets the XNX/XN masking logic in kvm_s2_trans_exec_el1(), which is the same area as the reported bug. Replacing the incorrect FIELD_PREP-style masking with a direct bitmask when FEAT_XNX is unsupported aligns with fixing the failure to clear XN[0] and thus is related to the vulnerability root cause.

candidates.rationale: This statement applies FIELD_PREP() to xn even though xn was already extracted with FIELD_GET(), so when FEAT_XNX is unavailable it masks against the wrong value and fails to clear the execute-never bit correctly.

The same incorrect masking logic appears in kvm_s2_trans_exec_el1(); using FIELD_PREP() here on an already-extracted bitfield causes the XN[0] clear operation to be ineffective when XNX is unsupported, leading to unintended execute permission.

vuln_statements.explanation: This line applies FIELD_PREP() to an already-extracted xn bitfield, so when FEAT_XNX is unavailable it masks the wrong value and fails to clear XN[0] correctly, which can leave execute permission enabled.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit d93febe2ed2e0491af9d47f0ee6d4b01918877f4
Author: Oliver Upton <oupton@kernel.org>
Date:   Mon Nov 24 11:01:45 2025 -0800

    KVM: arm64: nv: Forward FEAT_XNX permissions to the shadow stage-2
    
    Add support for FEAT_XNX to shadow stage-2 MMUs, being careful to only
    evaluate XN[0] when the feature is actually exposed to the VM.
    Restructure the layering of permissions in the fault handler to assume
    pX and uX then restricting based on the guest's stage-2 afterwards.
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown code does not contain the vulnerable construct anymore. The new helpers extract the already-decoded XN field with `u8 xn = FIELD_GET(KVM_PTE_LEAF_ATTR_HI_S2_XN, trans->desc);` and then only conditionally mask it when XNX is unavailable: `if (!kvm_has_xnx(kvm)) xn &= FIELD_PREP(KVM_PTE_LEAF_ATTR_HI_S2_XN, 0b10);`. The commit message also explicitly says it is adding FEAT_XNX support and is careful to only evaluate XN[0] when the feature is exposed. This indicates the prior incorrect handling has been replaced by feature-aware logic, so the vulnerable behavior is not present in this version.
